bullets: Charge on an electron = 1.6 × 10^{-19} C. Conventional current flows opposite to electron flow.
Ammeter goes **in series** (low resistance). Voltmeter goes **in parallel** (high resistance).
Ohm's law holds at constant temperature: the V–I graph is a straight line through the origin, and its slope gives R.
R depends on length (R ∝ L), area (R ∝ 1/A), material (ρ) and temperature. Doubling the length doubles R. Doubling the diameter makes R one-fourth.
Good conductors (Cu, Al) have low ρ. Alloys (nichrome) have high ρ and don't oxidise easily, so they are used in heaters, toasters and irons.
In parallel, R_{p} is smaller than the smallest resistor. A wire cut into n equal parts joined in parallel gives R/n^{2}.

box: **Why homes use parallel wiring:** each appliance gets the full 220 V, can be switched on or off separately, and keeps working if another fails.
**Uses of heating effect:** bulb filament (tungsten, very high melting point), electric iron, toaster, heater, fuse (low melting point wire).

bullets: Fridge 400 W × 8 h × 30 days = 96 kWh. At ₹3 per unit, the cost is ₹288.
Not converting units: mm → m (0.5 mm = 0.5 × 10^{-3} m), W → kW, minutes → seconds.
Using diameter instead of radius in A = πr^{2}.
Writing 'units' of energy without saying 1 unit = 1 kWh.
